name: Retail banking
one_line: Takes in deposits, lends them out at a higher rate, and keeps the spread.
sells: Checking and savings accounts, loans, mortgages, credit cards
suppliers: Depositors (the cheap money), card networks, core banking software

revenue.metric: net operating revenue of all FDIC-insured US banks
revenue.note: Net interest income $738.3B + noninterest income $337.8B. Covers all insured banks, so it overstates retail banking alone.

structure.why: Three banks hold about a third of US deposits; thousands of smaller banks share the rest.
structure.hhi_note: Shares are each bank's domestic deposits divided by ~$17.8T total domestic deposits (derived from FDIC Q2 2026: +$142.7B = +0.8%).

econ: Maturity transformation: banks borrow short (deposits you can withdraw today) and lend long (30-year mortgages). The spread is the profit; a run on deposits is the risk.
